question: Select the most appropriate option for blank (1)
solution:
The correct answer is** Option 4.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**were**" is the past tense plural form of the verb "to be" and is used here because it refers to the past situation of the initial two Russian PWR types at the Kudankulam site. (थे)
 
• The subject "initial two Russian PWR types" is plural, which requires the plural past tense verb **"were".**
 
• The other options: "**are**," "**is**," and "**was**" do not fit the context as appropriately. "Are" and "is" are present tense, and "was" is singular past tense.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *The initial two Russian PWR types at the Kudankulam site were__ apart from India's three-stage plan for nuclear power and were simply to increase generating capacity rapidly.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Are (हैं):** Present tense plural, not suitable for past actions.
 
• **Is (है):** Present tense singular, not suitable for both plurality and past action.
 
• **Was (था):** Past tense singular, not suitable for plural subjects.
